findings.title: Ophthalmology bedside consult (6 Nov 2026)
findings.detail: Asked to see for eye discharge the evening before surgery. Itching and discharge in both eyes for 2 days. Unaided visual acuity read as counting fingers at 3 m in each eye; eye movements full and painless; the patient finds it difficult to follow commands. Conjunctival congestion, greenish discharge at the fornix in both eyes, cornea appears clear, anterior chamber appears normal depth, pupil 3 mm reacting with no RAPD, lens written as SIMC. Impression: acute bacterial conjunctivitis. Two eye drops advised for both eyes for 2 weeks.

exceptions.title: Some hand-copied lab digits can be read two ways
exceptions.body: In the Medicine note of 5 Nov 2026 the writer's 5 and 3 look alike. Haemoglobin is taken as 12.5 because the Pulmonology note gives the same figure clearly. RBS (175 or 173), creatinine (0.5 and an unclear last digit), urea and TSH are less certain. None has a unit or range on the page.

exceptions.title: A circled value of 40 could not be identified
exceptions.body: In the Pulmonology note written after the 10 Nov request, a value of 40 is circled beside a three-letter label that looks like 'FBS' but could not be read with confidence. It is held back from the doctor's view. If it is a fasting sugar, it matters.

exceptions.title: Chest X-ray described differently by two teams
exceptions.body: Medicine (5 Nov) wrote left-sided homogenous opacification of the lung field. Pulmonology (6 Nov) wrote rotated film, cannot comment. There is no radiology report in this PDF.

exceptions.title: Sugar limit for surgery is overwritten
exceptions.body: Medicine's condition for surgery reads as pre-operative GRBS below 180 mg/dl, but the middle digit is written over and could be 150.

exceptions.title: Cardiology risk wording partly read
exceptions.body: The Cardiology advice reads 'can be taken up for planned Sx', then a mark like a down arrow and a struck-out word before 'added cardiac risk'. The level of risk meant is not certain.

exceptions.title: Pulmonology review of the saturation drop is undated and hard to read
exceptions.body: The reply to the 10 Nov request has no date or time and is in a difficult hand. BP is read as 170/80 (could be 120/80), the tramadol frequency and the 'SOB' mark are unclear, and the advice list skips number 3.

exceptions.title: Site of the old skin cancer is worded two ways
exceptions.body: Surgical Oncology writes SCC over the natal cleft. The requests and the other teams write right (upper) gluteal skin. Both describe the same 2017 excision.

exceptions.title: Eye drop frequency and one acuity line not read
exceptions.body: The Ophthalmology advice gives the frequency of the two eye drops as tally marks, which were not turned into a number. One line about visual acuity in the left eye could not be read.

normalLabs.names: TSH, uric acid, total bilirubin, direct bilirubin, total protein, albumin, globulin, AST, ALT, ALP, urea, lymphocytes, monocytes, AEC, coagulation (RFT, LFT and coagulation are marked N by the writers; the others are hand-copied without a range and are not flagged on the page)

timeline.title: Admitted under Orthopaedics, 4 pm
timeline.detail: Left femur neck fracture after a fall; left bipolar hemiarthroplasty planned.

timeline.title: Medicine and Surgical Oncology reviews
timeline.detail: SpO2 93% on 4 L oxygen. Surgery allowed once BP and sugar are controlled and after cardiac and pulmonology clearance. Old skin cancer site healthy.

timeline.title: Cardiology and Pulmonology work-up
timeline.detail: Echo EF 63%, ECG NSR. D-dimer 2.1, so CT pulmonary angiography advised.

timeline.title: Eye review, 7 pm
timeline.detail: Acute bacterial conjunctivitis in both eyes; drops for 2 weeks. Surgery posted for the next day.

timeline.title: Pulmonology clearance under high risk
timeline.detail: CTPA: no acute embolism, basal atelectasis. SpO2 86% on room air, 96% on 4 L.

timeline.title: Pulmonology review, 5:45 pm
timeline.detail: SpO2 98% on 6 L by face mask. Nebulisation, oxygen, chest physiotherapy, incentive spirometry.

timeline.title: Oxygen saturation drop
timeline.detail: SpO2 90% on room air, pulse 105. ? Volume overload / basal atelectasis; NT-proBNP and strict intake/output advised. Hb 10.1.

timeline.title: Discharged
timeline.detail: Discharge slip dated 12/11/26; no transfusion recorded.

timeline.title: Admitted under Medicine
timeline.detail: Provisional diagnosis left lower lobe pneumonia; expected stay 7 days.

timeline.title: 2D echo requested
timeline.detail: Request to Cardiology at 9 am; no reply on the page.

notes: The text layer is unusable OCR of handwriting; all 19 pages were read from the image. Each consultation record is scanned with its back page first: 33 is the back of 34 (Medicine), 35 of 36 (Ophthalmology), 37 of 38 (Surgical Oncology), 39 of 40 (Cardiology), 45 of 46 (Pulmonology, 6 Nov). Pages 42-43 are one sheet used twice: page 43 holds the 7 Nov 5:45 pm request and reply and, at the bottom, the 10 Nov request; page 42 is the undated reply to it (the '(D4)' beside Augmentin fits 10 Nov). The 10 Nov date on the vitals, labs and impression from page 42 is therefore inferred from the request, not written on the reply. Page 41 is a blank back. The operation itself is not documented here: these pages say 'planned' and 'posted tomorrow' (6 Nov), and F1's ICU chart starts on 7 Nov, so the merger should take the procedure date from an operation note in F5/F6 if there is one. The 5 Nov ED visit that led to this admission is ER-2026-11-05 in F2; the May ED visit is ER-2026-05-15 in F2. The medicines under 'On Rx' in the Medicine note of 5 Nov are filed as home medicines with an 'ambiguous' flag because the page does not say home or ward; F5/F6 may have a reconciliation form that settles it. T2DM and HTN share one cited line. The May admission label on page 51 prints the age as 83 Y, while the May ED labels in F2 print 84 Y; 84 is used as the latest. The I.P. numbers on the two admission orders are used only as encounter refs. Names of doctors, the patient and the relative named on the consent sections were left out. All lab values are hand-copied by residents; abnormal 'H' is set only where the writer circled the value and the direction is not in doubt (TLC, neutrophils, ESR, D-dimer).
